title: Schema disable/delete: schedule handling, coupled flags, and in-flight teardown
answers: What must change when a schema's should_sync is turned off?
Which schedules are paused vs deleted on schema/source delete?
How does auto_disabled_at relate to should_sync?
What tears down running syncs when a schema is disabled?
body:
- Non-CDC schema: per-schema schedule (id = schema id) is paused on disable/unpaused on enable by `ExternalDataSchema.update_should_sync` (only if `source.supports_scheduled_sync`); creates schedule if missing and should_sync=True. `to_temporal_schedule`/`get_sync_schedule` in data_load/service.py set `paused=not should_sync`.
- Deleted source/schema: schedules are DELETED, not paused: source `destroy` (source_setup.py) → `bulk_delete_external_data_schedules`, `delete_external_data_schedule(source.id)`, `delete_discover_schemas_schedule(source.id)`. DB soft-delete (source, schemas, tables, _cdc tables) is one `transaction.atomic()`; schedule/S3 cleanup is after, best-effort.
- Coupled flags: `auto_disabled_at` stamped in `ExternalDataSchema.save()` via `_apply_auto_disabled_marker` only under `sync_disable_context(error_message=...)`; user disable leaves None; re-enable clears. `ExternalDataSchemaQuerySet.update` clears it on any bulk write naming should_sync. Digest uses `SCHEMA_STOPPED_BY_USER` (notifications.py). `deleted`+`deleted_at` set together (`soft_delete`, bulk update in destroy). `delete_table()` resets table_id/last_synced_at/status to None.
- Teardown: `save()` → `_sync_teardown_kind` → `_schedule_sync_teardown`, and the QuerySet.update path (bulk bypasses save), dispatch Celery `cleanup_disabled_external_data_schema` on commit only on real transition and if a Running job exists. Task aborts if schema is re-enabled. `teardown_schema_syncs` (sync_teardown.py): fail job, fail queue batches/release v3 lock, release expired leases, cancel workflow (skip `exclude_workflow_id`). `sweep_stopped_schema_syncs` is the backstop.
applies: Disabling via should_sync or soft-delete; auto-disable path passes disable_exclude_workflow_id (external_data_job.py) so the run doesn't cancel itself.
